**STEP 1 - Scene:** This is a small snack of whole almonds (shelled, roasted-looking) on a white square plate. The photo is taken from directly above.

**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The square plate spans roughly 350 px. An almond is about 2.5 cm long and measures about 35 px, so the scale is about 14 px/cm. That makes the plate about 24-25 cm across, a dinner-plate size. I use 24 cm, so area = 3.14 × 12² ≈ 452 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** About 17 whole almonds. No oil, sauce, or dressing is visible.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The almonds sit in a loose cluster in the centre-right of the plate, covering about 12-15% of the plate area (roughly 60 cm²).

**STEP 5 - Volume:** The almonds lie mostly flat, with a few stacked, so the pile averages about 1.2 cm high. Gross volume ≈ 60 cm² × 1.2 cm ≈ 72 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Counting pieces is more reliable than volume here. A shelled almond weighs about 1.2 g, so 17 almonds ≈ 20 g. The volume route (72 ml × ~0.5 g/ml) gives a similar figure of roughly 35 g, which would mean the almonds are on the small side. I take about 20 g as the best estimate.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Almonds are about 579 kcal/100 g. 20 g × 5.79 ≈ 116 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** Seventeen almonds is a modest handful, so about 20 g and about 115 kcal is plausible. This is a light snack, not a full meal.
